Article Title: Oil prices extend losses as Hormuz reopening hopes ease supply fears
Article Text:
Brent crude fell 0.5% to $87.43 a barrel

Oil prices extended their decline on Thursday as hopes of renewed Middle East diplomacy raised expectations that the Strait of Hormuz could reopen, easing concerns over prolonged supply disruptions.Brent crude fell 0.5 per cent to $87.43 a barrel, heading for a fourth straight session of losses, while US West Texas Intermediate crude dropped 0.5 per cent to $81.86, on track for a fifth day of declines.The selling followed reports that Iran and Oman were working to finalise an agreement concerning the Strait of Hormuz, a critical energy route that handled oil and gas shipments equivalent to about one-fifth of global fuel consumption before the conflict began.Qatar's prime minister is also due to travel to Iran on Thursday to revive diplomatic talks aimed at ending the nearly six-month-old conflict. The US has halted attacks on Iran for about a month, while seeking greater economic pressure on Tehran.However, uncertainty over the waterway remains. Iran has indicated that Hormuz would not fully reopen unless the US meets its conditions under a ceasefire arrangement that later broke down.Analysts said the continued risk to shipping means a war premium could remain embedded in oil prices.Supply concerns are also emerging in diesel markets. US distillate inventories, which include diesel and heating oil, fell by 2.2 million barrels in the week to August 21, reaching their lowest seasonal level on record, according to the US Energy Information Administration.
Article Summary: Brent crude fell 0.5% to $87.43 a barrel, heading for a fourth straight session of losses. US West Texas Intermediate crude dropped 0. 5 per cent to $81.86. Selling followed reports that Iran and Oman were working to finalise an agreement concerning the Strait of Hormuz.

Article Title: Bank holiday today: Are banks open or closed on August 26 for Id-E-Milad? Check state-wise details
Article Text:
Bank operations will vary state to state on Wednesday

Can you still use banking services?

When will banks remain closed next?

If you are planning to visit a bank branch on Wednesday, August 26, you may need to reschedule your visit depending on where you live. Bank branches in several cities will remain closed today for Id-E-Milad, Milad-un-Nabi and Thiruvonam, while branches in other parts of the country will operate as usual.According to the Reserve Bank of India’s holiday calendar, banks will remain closed in Belapur, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Chennai, Dehradun, Hyderabad, Imphal, Jammu, Kanpur, Kochi, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, New Delhi, Patna, Raipur, Ranchi, Srinagar and Thiruvananthapuram.The closures are linked to Id-E-Milad/Baravafat/Milad-un-Nabi, with Thiruvonam also observed in Kerala. The holiday is therefore not applicable to bank branches across the country.A bank holiday affects physical branch operations but does not mean that all banking services stop. Customers can continue using ATMs, UPI, internet banking and mobile banking for most routine transactions, subject to scheduled maintenance.However, services requiring a physical branch visit, such as document submission, verification or certain account-related requests, will not be available at closed branches.Customers should check their specific branch's holiday calendar before visiting, as bank holidays can vary by city and state.Banks across India will remain closed on Sunday, August 30, as part of the regular Sunday holiday. The next major state-specific closures after August 26 are scheduled for August 28, when branches in several centres will close for Raksha Bandhan and other regional observances.
Article Summary: Banks will remain closed in Belapur, Bengaluru, Bhopal, Chennai, Dehradun, Hyderabad, Imphal, Jammu, Kanpur, Kochi, Lucknow, Mumbai, Nagpur, New Delhi, Patna, Raipur, Ranchi, Srinagar and Thiruvananthapuram. The closures are linked to Id-E-Milad/Baravafat/Milad-un-Nabi, with Thiruvonam also observed in Kerala.

Article Title: 'A whole new vibe': Ashwini Vaishnaw shares glimpse of bullet train project taking shape
Article Text:
Ashwini Vaishnaw shares glimpse of bullet train project taking shape

India’s first bullet train is slowly moving from plans to pillars. Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on Tuesday shared a glimpse of the work taking shape across Thane and Palghar, calling it, "a whole new vibe!" The 135.45-km elevated section stretches from Shilphata in Thane district to Zaroli village on the Maharashtra-Gujarat border.The route cuts through varied terrain, with 124.027 km of the section comprising viaducts and bridges, the National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) said in an official release on Tuesday.The construction is at different stages along the stretch. Pier work is underway across more than 100 km, while nearly 74 km of piers have been completed and are ready for viaduct girders.The work is being supported by nine casting yards, seven full-span launching gantries and eight SBS launching gantries, all currently operational in Maharashtra.Three elevated stations are also coming up along the stretch: Thane, Virar and Boisar. The Thane station has a concourse level around 12 metres above the natural ground level, a design aimed at protecting and preserving local mangroves in the eco-sensitive zone.The tunnels are making progress too. Of the seven planned mountain tunnels on the section, three have already achieved breakthrough, with drainage, waterproofing and lining work now underway.Bridges are another key part of the stretch, including a 460-metre bridge over the Ulhas River, a 2.32-km bridge over the Vaitarna River and a 510-metre bridge over the Jagani River.Overall, the section will have 36 bridges and crossings, including 12 steel bridges over major railway lines, the Mumbai-Nashik Highway and the Ulhas River.The release said the progress reflects the engineering work behind the project under Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision and Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw’s drive to expand next-generation railway infrastructure.
Article Summary: Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw shared a glimpse of the work taking shape across Thane and Palghar. The 135.45-km elevated section stretches from Shilphata in Thane district to Zaroli village on the Maharashtra-Gujarat border. Three elevated stations are also coming up along the stretch: Thane, Virar and Boisar.

Article Title: Stock market operations on August 26: Are NSE, BSE open or closed today for Eid-e-Milad?
Article Text:
Stock markets have been quite volatile this week

So, is the stock market closed today?

What does a settlement holiday mean?

With Eid-e-Milad being observed on Wednesday, August 26, investors may be wondering whether they will get a trading holiday on the stock market. The festival is a holiday for several government offices and institutions, and banks in many states are also closed. But the stock market follows a separate holiday calendar.No. The NSE and BSE will remain open for regular equity trading on August 26, allowing investors to buy and sell shares during normal market hours.However, the day is a holiday for trade settlement.This means trading will continue as normal, but the clearing and settlement of funds and securities will not take place on the day.In simple terms, investors can buy and sell shares, but the actual transfer of securities or funds linked to eligible trades may be pushed to the next settlement day. Investors expecting shares or sale proceeds should therefore factor in the one-day settlement delay.The distinction is important because a trading holiday means the market is shut, while a settlement holiday allows trading to continue but pauses the settlement process.The currency market will remain closed on August 26, while commodity exchanges such as MCX and NCDEX will operate.The next full trading holiday for the Indian stock market is September 14 for Ganesh Chaturthi.
Article Summary: NSE and BSE will remain open for regular equity trading on August 26. However, the day is a holiday for trade settlement. This means trading will continue as normal, but the clearing and settlement of funds and securities will not take place on the day.

Article Title: Oil prices today: Crude holds steady, heads for weekly losses as Hormuz flows remain choppy
Article Text:
Goldman Sachs estimated that total Gulf exports recently stood at 15 million to 16 million barrels per day (representative image)

Hormuz traffic remains uneven

MCX crude slips nearly 1%

Oil prices were largely steady on Friday but remained on track for a sharp weekly decline as traders weighed stalled US-Iran diplomatic talks against a tentative and uneven recovery in crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz.Brent crude futures were down 4 cents at $89.66 a barrel at 0943 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude fell 32 cents, or 0.38%, to $83.21 a barrel.Both benchmarks were set to end the week lower, with Brent down 5.1% and WTI declining 4.5%.“A combination of US tactics moving to economic sanctions rather than military pressure and talks of Oman-Iran's joint corridor have led to risk premiums declining,” Suvro Sarkar, head of energy research at DBS Bank, told Reuters.The US announced what it called the “toughest sanctions in history” on Iran earlier this week. Tehran described the sanctions as an “inhumane and hostile act” that had lost their effectiveness.The Strait of Hormuz, through which around 20% of the world's oil supply moves, has seen a tentative recovery in shipping, although flows remain uneven.Preliminary shipping data showed that seven commodity vessels transited the waterway on Thursday, down from 17 a day earlier and below the 10-day average of 15, Reuters reported.At the Bab el-Mandeb, another major maritime chokepoint, 17 commodity vessels passed through, with six entering and 11 exiting.Goldman Sachs estimated that total Gulf exports recently stood at 15 million to 16 million barrels per day, around 7 million to 8 million bpd below pre-war levels but 5 million to 6 million bpd above the lowest point recorded in March.“We are of the attitude of being prepared for everything but predicting nothing,” PVM Oil Futures analyst John Evans said, adding that several factors, including OPEC developments and China's demand, remained linked to the wider conflict.In India, crude oil futures also traded lower on Friday. Crude futures for September delivery on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) fell Rs 49, or nearly 1%, to Rs 7,915 per barrel.The October contract declined Rs 56, or 0.71%, to Rs 7,797 per barrel.Analysts cited by news agency PTI said that reports of a possible US role in Venezuela's oil industry weighed on prices as traders assessed the possibility of increased output from the South American producer.Anindya Banerjee, head of commodity and currency research at Kotak Securities, said Brent was trading lower as Washington's shift from military to economic pressure had reduced fears of a wider war.He added that Iran and Oman had reached a partial arrangement on sharing revenue from Hormuz traffic, although Tehran has said a full deal remains blocked.“The easing in prices reflects a market moving away from extreme conditions, although the underlying supply remains tight,” Banerjee said.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures were down 4 cents at $89.66 a barrel at 0943 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude fell 32 cents, or 0.38%, to $83.21 a barrel. Both benchmarks were set to end the week lower, with Brent down 5.1% and WTI declining 4.5%.

Article Title: Government achieves 78% of FY27 disinvestment, asset monetisation target in 5 months
Article Text:
Taken together, capital receipts from disinvestment and asset monetisation stand at Rs 62,124 crore (representative image)

LIC stake sale contributes more than half

IDBI Bank sale remains on the table

Targets have varied over the years

The government has achieved about 78% of its FY27 budgeted target of Rs 80,000 crore for disinvestment and asset monetisation within the first five months of the financial year.The government has raised Rs 55,757 crore so far through minority stake sales in nine public sector undertakings, strategic sale of Indian Medicines Pharmaceuticals Corporation Ltd and remittances from SUUTI.In addition, Rs 6,367 crore has been raised through asset monetisation via InvITs.Taken together, capital receipts from disinvestment and asset monetisation stand at Rs 62,124 crore, or around 78% of the full-year Budget target.More than half of the disinvestment proceeds came from the government's 6.5% stake sale in Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), which fetched Rs 31,515 crore.A 2% stake sale in Coal India raised around Rs 5,542 crore, while a 6.01% stake dilution in NHPC brought in Rs 4,357 crore.Earlier this week, the government sold a 6% stake in Hindustan Copper, raising Rs 3,041 crore.Other public sector entities in which the government diluted its stake include Central Bank of India, NLC India, GIC, IRFC and Cochin Shipyard, besides Hindustan Copper.The government is also pursuing the strategic sale of IDBI Bank.After an earlier attempt to sell the bank failed this year, the government has received revised bids from Dubai-based Emirates NDB and Prem Watsa-led Fairfax Financial Holdings, according to news agency PTI.The push to raise miscellaneous capital receipts through disinvestment and asset monetisation comes amid concerns that government expenditure could exceed Budget estimates due to higher energy and fertiliser import bills.The government has set a fiscal deficit target of 4.3% of GDP for FY27.The government stopped fixing separate disinvestment targets from the Revised Estimates of FY2023-24. Instead, amounts have been budgeted under Miscellaneous Capital Receipts.The amount budgeted stood at Rs 30,000 crore for RE FY2023-24, Rs 33,000 crore for RE FY2024-25, Rs 33,837 crore for RE FY2025-26, and Rs 80,000 crore for BE FY2026-27.In FY2021-22 and FY2022-23, the government raised Rs 13,534 crore and Rs 35,294 crore, respectively, against Revised Estimate targets of Rs 78,000 crore and Rs 50,000 crore.In FY2019-20 and FY2020-21, actual realisation stood at Rs 50,300 crore and Rs 32,886 crore, respectively, against Revised Estimate targets of Rs 65,000 crore and Rs 32,000 crore.
Article Summary: The government has raised Rs 55,757 crore so far through minority stake sales in nine public sector undertakings, strategic sale of Indian Medicines Pharmaceuticals Corporation Ltd and remittances from SUUTI. More than half of the disinvestment proceeds came from the government's 6.5% stake sale in Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC)

Article Title: IndiGo Ventures invests in Sarvam to enhance Artificial Intelligence in aviation
Article Text:
File photo: IndiGo

NEW DELHI: IndiGo Ventures, IndiGo’s corporate VC arm, will invest an undisclosed amount in Sarvam, India’s full-stack sovereign AI company, as part of Sarvam’s Series B round of funding. Announced Friday, the investment builds on the existing relationship between IndiGo and Sarvam who have been working together in multiple areas like enhancing customer experience and streamlining complex operational workflows across the airline through AI technologies.Neetan Chopra, IndiGo’s chief digital and information officer, said: “Artificial Intelligence is fast becoming a foundational capability for the aviation industry, reshaping customer experience, workforce productivity and operational decision-making.Our partnership with Sarvam gives IndiGo access to cutting-edge AI capabilities, built in India, and tailored to the needs of the market. By combining these technologies with our operational expertise and scale, we can accelerate innovation while maximising value for our customers, employees, and other stakeholders.”Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar said: “Aviation is a powerful setting for enterprise AI because it combines millions of customer interactions with complex, time-sensitive operations.IndiGo brings the domain depth and scale needed to identify where AI can create real value. Together, we can develop systems that are useful in production and build a stronger template for enterprise AI in India.”In a joint statement, the two companies said: “Aviation brings together high volumes of customer interactions, time-sensitive operations and a large, distributed workforce. The collaboration combines IndiGo’s core aviation expertise, operational scale and real-world use cases with Sarvam’s capabilities across AI models, voice and agentic systems to create a technology enabled, modern and future-ready airline infrastructure. IndiGo and Sarvam will continue to develop and evaluate applications across customer experience, employee productivity and airline operations, with the ability to expand successful use cases across IndiGo’s network.”IndiGo Ventures had three years ago received SEBI approval to establish an alternative investment fund (AIF) with a corpus of Rs 600 crore which is “committed to fostering innovation.”
Article Summary: IndiGo Ventures, IndiGo’s corporate VC arm, will invest an undisclosed amount in Sarvam. The investment builds on the existing relationship between the two companies. The two companies will continue to develop and evaluate applications across customer experience, employee productivity and airline operations.

Article Title: From Suez to Russia’s Arctic: Why India, China are betting on Northern Sea Route & why it matters
Article Text:
India is planning to send its first cargo ship through the Northern Sea Route in 2027.

Crucial Energy Bottlenecks at the centre of Middle East crisis

What is the Northern Sea Route?

How Northern Sea Route Works For China

China already using NSR

What India is planning on NSR

Northern Sea Route- What India & Russia are exploring

What changes for India?

Northern Sea Route: India's Bet on Arctic Route

What Bhavik Vora from Grant Thornton Bharat said

Why it’s important

NSR Constraints & What They Mean For India

What EY's Agneshwar Sen said

Donald Trump’s trade and tariff policies, sanctions risks, and the ongoing Middle East route disruptions have led economies like India to reassess their supply chain strategies. The US-Iran war and the Houthi attacks in the Red Sea have exposed trade route vulnerabilities like never before. And some of the world’s largest economies like China, India and Japan are reassessing their trade route dependencies.With the Strait of Hormuz, Red Sea and Suez Canal routes facing disruptions, the Northern Sea Route is in focus for Asia’s trade with Russia and Europe.The Northern Sea Route (NSR), a frozen area route cutting through the Arctic along Russia’s northern coast, is now being used by China, and soon India will join the club.The attraction is clear: The trade route cuts distance and travel time significantly. But the NSR is not without its challenges.India’s interest in the Northern Sea Route is being shaped by two factors: its commercial potential and the need to broaden trade connectivity. The NSR also offers a clear geographical advantage on certain Asia-Europe trade lanes, especially routes linking Asian ports with northern Europe.However, the economic potential of the route has to be weighed against the added challenges of operating in the Arctic. Can NSR replace Suez Canal as a meaningful alternative trade route? Let’s take a look:The Northern Sea Route is a link between Russia’s western ports with Asian markets via the Arctic waters. It’s a seasonal route that usually remains open through July-September every year.It’s over 5,500 km long shipping passage along Russia’s Arctic coast and the reason it has been gaining importance is due to the disruption of traditional trade routes like the Strait of Hormuz and Suez canal.Russia is investing in the infrastructure needed to turn the NSR into a major international trade corridor.It’s important because it allows Russia to ship cargo to China and other parts of Asia without any possible inspections and detentions related to Ukraine-related sanctions.Reports suggest that Russia’s crude oil shipping via the Arctic Sea has picked up pace this year. Reuters recently reported that seven cargoes with around 6 million barrels of crude were dispatched for Asia.While India, Japan and South Korea have expressed interest in the Northern Sea Route, China has moved fast and is already receiving shipments through it.In fact, traders are already anticipating that China will step up shipments through the route if Iranian oil supplies remain disrupted due to the Middle East conflict.The NSR helps reduce the travel time to China by about two weeks if one were to compare it to the usual route. Traders have said that China is the biggest beneficiary from this particular route since its ports are closer to the Far Eastern export terminals of Russia.For China the route is reduced from 40 days via the Suez canal to just 18 days to the United Kingdom.Experts say China is emerging as an early commercial beneficiary, building on its long-standing “Polar Silk Road” ambitions with Russia.Rosatom, which operates the NSR and provides nuclear-powered icebreakers, has issued permits for seven Chinese vessels travelling to Europe, with ships planned to sail weekly during the 2026 navigation season.India is planning to send its first cargo ship through the Northern Sea Route in 2027.Discussions with Russia's Arkhangelsk region are being held for the use of ports for Indian exports and imports, shipbuilding and potentially locating production near ports.There are added benefits as well: the region offers access to hydrocarbons, LNG, nickel, copper, platinum, palladium and rare earths.From India’s perspective, the NSR would complement the trade relationship with Moscow, while also providing an alternative to the Chennai-Vladivostok Eastern Maritime Corridor, which has seen cargo movement rise 70%.“India's approach appears to be moving from strategic assessment towards practical evaluation. The government is planning India's first pilot cargo voyage through the NSR in 2027,” Bhavik Vora, Partner and Transport and Logistics industry leader, Grant Thornton Bharat tells TOI.“This is significant because the commercial viability of the route will ultimately depend on actual operating economics rather than the theoretical distance advantage. The pilot should provide an opportunity to assess transit times, vessel requirements, insurance, navigation support, port infrastructure, and the economics of different cargo categories,” he says.The NSR is distinct from the Chennai-Vladivostok Eastern Maritime Corridor which directly connects India’s east coast with Russia’s Far East and has already demonstrated how to cut the India-Far East Russia journey from around 40 days to about 24 days.Estimates suggest that for India the Northern Sea Route would lead to the number of days for travel to Europe reducing by about 40% or two weeks.Experts believe that both geopolitical concerns and economics will drive India’s strategy with regards to the route. Also, even though geopolitical events-led disruptions may result in the shift, economics is what will decide whether India walks through it.According to Kpler data, Russian crude exports to India are dominated by Black Sea (Novorossiysk) and Baltic (Primorsk, Ust Luga) loadings, which together made up around 88% of Russia-India crude volumes in July 2026, compared with under 8% from the Arctic port of Murmansk.Matthew Wright, Senior Manager - Freight, Kpler tells TOI that even as India is interested in the NSR, it can only ever be relevant to a small slice of the trade.“For that slice, the NSR isn't faster or shorter than Suez, it's about 3.5 days slower and 1,100 nmi longer, so the appeal isn't economic. What it does offer is reduced risk around the Bab-el Mandeb and avoided SECA compliance costs. That points to interest being driven by risk diversification rather than genuine cost or time advantage, and even then only for a minority of the cargo,” he says.Red Sea disruptions, since late 2023, have already forced re-routing of shipping around the Cape of Good Hope, adding cost and time to India-Europe trade.From a crude oil perspective, very little would change for India, says Kpler’s Matthew Wright.“The overwhelming majority of Russian crude reaching India loads from Black Sea and Baltic ports, and that cargo is naturally routed via Suez or around Europe regardless of what the NSR offers, since it isn't anywhere near the Arctic route,” he says.Agneshwar Sen, Trade Policy Leader, EY India says India is interested in any route that reduces dependence on chokepoints such as Suez, Hormuz, Malacca.“Thus, it is really a combination of economics and the need for supply chain resilience. The NSR, for selected Asia-Europe trade, can reduce sailing distance by roughly 30-40% compared with the Suez route,” he explains.But distance is not the only factor, the biggest constraint will be the cost of shipping and associated risks.Ice-class vessels, icebreaker support, insurance, navigation constraints and seasonality can offset a significant part of the savings, Sen tells TOI.Bhavik Vora of Grant Thornton Bharat is of the view that the NSR could alter the economics and resilience of India's trade with Russia and selected European markets by providing a shorter maritime connection for certain origin-destination pairs.However, he notes that its relevance will differ considerably between India-Russia and India-Europe trade.“For India-Russia trade, the NSR complements rather than replaces India's other connectivity initiatives, including the Chennai-Vladivostok Eastern Maritime Corridor and the International North-South Transport Corridor. The route could improve access to Russia's northern and Arctic regions and support the movement of energy, minerals, and other bulk commodities,” Bhavik Vora says.This is particularly relevant given the scale and composition of bilateral trade: India–Russia trade was $59.9 billion in FY2025–26, of which Indian imports were $55.4 billion.Russian supplies to India include petroleum products, fertilisers, coking coal, and vegetable oils, while Indian exports include pharmaceuticals, chemicals, iron and steel and marine products.According to Vora, for Europe, the opportunity is more selective.“The NSR is naturally better suited to northern European destinations than to the whole of Europe, and its distance advantage is therefore highly dependent on the specific port pair,” he tells TOI.Commercial activity in 2026 is beginning to demonstrate this potential. A Chinese operator has launched a scheduled Arctic container service from Ningbo to Felixstowe, with eight sailings planned for the 2026 season and an expected transit of around 20 days. The service is scheduled to operate from August through October.“The strategic implication for India is that the NSR could eventually form part of a multi-corridor trade architecture, where shippers select between Suez, the Cape route, the NSR and land-based corridors depending on cost, time, security, and cargo characteristics. It should not, however, be treated as a risk-free alternative. The NSR introduces its own dependencies, particularly on Russian infrastructure and regulatory arrangements,” he cautions.The biggest factor and benefit is route diversification for trade, which has become important in today’s uncertain geopolitical and trade environment. It is key to supply chain resilience.“This is also consistent with the broader India-Russia approach to connectivity. The two countries have explicitly identified the Chennai-Vladivostok Eastern Maritime Corridor, the INSTC (where India has Chabahar port included as an alternative to Bandar Abbas) and the potential of the Northern Sea Route as complementary elements of a more diversified Eurasian transportation architecture,” EY’s Sen says.According to Agneshwar Sen, NSR can have a significant impact on the energy and bulk cargo side since it shortens the route between Russian Arctic/ Far East ports and India, complementing the Chennai-Vladivostok Eastern Maritime Corridor and the INSTC, and gives India a third artery for crude, LNG, coal and fertiliser.For India-Europe trade, the benefits may be more long-term. While the NSR would in principle cut sailing distance to northern Europe by up to 40% and transit time by about two weeks versus Suez, it isn’t as yet a corridor for the India-Europe container or general cargo trade, which needs reliable, high-frequency, container-ready service, he says.For India, therefore, the immediate strategic value of the NSR is not a cheaper route but that it can provide an additional routing option for specific trade flows.“Building that option has value in itself as global trade becomes more exposed to geopolitical and infrastructure-related disruptions,” says Bhavik Vora.But, what prevents the Northern Sea Route from becoming a full-time substitute is its seasonality. So, its role as a substitute for the Suez Canal is limited, feel experts.The thick ice in the Arctic region means that specialised ice-strengthened vessels and nuclear-powered icebreakers are required for navigation through it.High operating costs, safety concerns, sanctions, limited infrastructure and environmental risks remain significant constraints. Shrinking summer sea ice is widening the navigation window, but experts caution that the NSR cannot currently substitute for Suez or Hormuz.Three structural constraints keep the role limited according to the EY expert:(i) navigability is still limited to a few ice-free months without heavy icebreaker escort, versus Suez’s year-round, weather-independent service;(ii) the NSR is used for bulk and tanker cargo, not the container liner traffic that dominates India-Europe trade, and container infrastructure/ ports along the route are thin;(iii) sanctions risk, which limits the pool of vessels and underwriters willing to service it.“Nonetheless, it can become a meaningful supplementary corridor for specific bulk commodities and a hedge against Suez/Red Sea disruption, but “Suez alternative” implies scale and reliability the NSR currently doesn’t offer,” Agneshwar Sen says.As Bhavik Vora concludes: The NSR is moving beyond the stage of being purely experimental, but it is still too early to consider it a substitute for Suez. The more credible scenario is that it develops into a complementary corridor for selected trade lanes and cargo categories, especially from the Asian part of Russia.Scale remains the principal constraint. Major shipping companies are beginning to selectively restore Suez services as security conditions improve. This means the NSR cannot rely indefinitely on disruption to Suez to generate demand.“For the route to become structurally relevant to India, it will need to demonstrate competitive economics and sufficient reliability even when conventional routes are operating normally. Its likely role over the medium term is therefore a seasonal and strategically valuable alternative rather than a replacement for Suez,” he says.
Article Summary: The Northern Sea Route (NSR) is a frozen area route cutting through the Arctic along Russia’s northern coast. China is already using the route, and soon India will join the club. The attraction is clear: The trade route cuts distance and travel time significantly. But the NSR is not without its challenges.

Article Title: Jio Platforms gets Sebi nod for $3.8 billion IPO, potentially India’s biggest listing
Article Text:
$3.8 billion Jio IPO gets Sebi approval

Fresh share sale, debt repayment plans

One of the world's largest mobile operators

Jio Platforms, the digital services arm of Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Industries , has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) for its proposed $3.8 billion initial public offering, paving the way for what could become India’s biggest listing.The market regulator approved the IPO on Friday, marking a key step that allows the company to proceed with further preparations for the public issue, subject to regulatory requirements.Jio Platforms had filed its draft papers with Sebi in June for the proposed IPO, which is expected to raise around $4 billion, or approximately Rs 37,700 crore.According to the draft prospectus, Jio Platforms plans to offer up to 27 crore fresh equity shares, representing around 2.9% of its total equity base after the issue.The company plans to use most of the IPO proceeds to reduce debt at its telecom unit, Reliance Jio Infocomm. As per Reuters, around Rs 275 billion, or $3.3 billion, of the proceeds would be used to repay Reliance Jio Infocomm's debt.The public issue is structured as a primary share sale, meaning the company will retain the proceeds rather than existing shareholders selling their stakes through an offer-for-sale.Reliance Jio had 524.4 million subscribers at the end of March, making it the world's largest mobile operator by single-country subscriber base after China Mobile.The company reported a roughly 21% decline in headcount to 27,935 employees during the year ended March 31, even as its revenue and subscriber numbers continued to grow.The listing comes amid a revival in India's primary market. More than two dozen IPOs have been launched or announced in less than two months since July 1, nearly matching the 28 IPOs recorded in the first half of 2026.The proposed listing would mark a major milestone for Jio Platforms and could potentially surpass previous public issues to become the largest IPO in India's history.
Article Summary: Jio Platforms, the digital services arm of Mukesh Ambani-led Reliance Industries, has received approval from the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) for its proposed $3.8 billion initial public offering. The company plans to use most of the IPO proceeds to reduce debt at its telecom unit, Reliance Jio Infocomm.

Article Title: Meta’s Sandhya Devanathan exits after decade, joins OpenAI as Southeast Asia, Australia VP
Article Text:
Sandhya Devanathan, VP, Southeast Asia and Australia, OpenAI

BENGALURU

: Meta’s vice-president for India and Southeast Asia Sandhya Devanathan is leaving the social media giant after more than a decade to join OpenAI , where she will become vice-president for Southeast Asia and Australia.Devanathan will be based in Singapore and report to Kiran Mani, OpenAI’s managing director for Asia-Pacific. The newly created position makes her the ChatGPT maker’s most senior executive across Southeast Asia and Australia. OpenAI confirmed the development.Her remit will span consumer growth, enterprise adoption and partnerships, regulatory engagement and operations. She will also focus on building partnerships across the AI ecosystem and expanding the use of OpenAI’s products among businesses, institutions and government bodies in the region.Devanathan announced her departure from Meta in a LinkedIn post on Friday, describing it as a “bittersweet decision” after more than a decade at the company. She said she would take a short break before beginning her next chapter.She joined Meta in 2016 and held a string of leadership positions across Asia-Pacific, including running its regional gaming business and helping expand the company’s presence in Singapore and Vietnam.She was named Meta’s India head in late 2022 and later took on responsibility for Southeast Asia as well.Devanathan, who has more than 25 years of experience across technology and financial services, recalled joining Meta when it had around 300 employees in Singapore. During her stint, she worked across ecommerce and gaming and led teams serving businesses, creators and users across India and Southeast Asia.In her farewell post, she highlighted Meta’s work with government citizen services on WhatsApp in India, small businesses using its platforms in Vietnam, Indonesia and Thailand, and startups across Singapore, Malaysia and the Philippines.Her appointment comes as OpenAI steps up its presence across Asia-Pacific amid rising adoption of generative AI by consumers, developers and enterprises. Over the past two years, the company has opened offices in Singapore, Tokyo, Seoul, Sydney and Delhi.OpenAI has also been adding senior regional executives. Mani was recently appointed to lead Asia-Pacific, while Prabhjeet Singh is set to head its India business.The move makes Devanathan one of the most senior Meta executives in the region to cross over to the fast-growing generative AI sector.
Article Summary: Sandhya Devanathan will be based in Singapore and report to Kiran Mani, OpenAI’s managing director for Asia-Pacific. Her remit will span consumer growth, enterprise adoption and partnerships, regulatory engagement and operations. She has more than 25 years of experience across technology and financial services.

Article Title: India expresses readiness for treaty talks with Canada, eyes Rs 4.65 lakh crore trade
Article Text:
India expresses readiness to initiate negotiations on Bilateral Investment Treaty with Canada; aim Rs 4.65 lakh crore trade by 2030

India ready to begin investment treaty talks

Trade target set at CAD 70 billion

UPI and financial cooperation

Focus on critical minerals

India-Canada trade and CEPA talks

India has offered to begin talks with Canada on a Bilateral Investment Treaty at the earliest, as both countries look to deepen economic ties and increase bilateral trade to CAD 70 billion, or INR 4.65 lakh crore, by 2030.The proposal came during the first Canada-India Finance Ministers' Economic and Financial Dialogue, where Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman met her Canadian counterpart Francois-Philippe Champagne.The two ministers discussed ways to strengthen trade and investment ties and agreed on several areas of economic cooperation."India expressed its readiness to initiate negotiations on a Bilateral Investment Treaty at the earliest," the joint statement issued after the meeting said.A Bilateral Investment Treaty is an agreement between two countries designed to provide greater protection and certainty to investors from both sides.The meeting followed a commitment made by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi in March 2026 to improve economic and financial cooperation.The two countries have also agreed to work towards completing negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement by the end of 2026.Sitharaman and Champagne reaffirmed their goal of taking bilateral trade between India and Canada to "CAD 70 billion / INR 4.65 lakh crore by 2030."They also welcomed the increasing investment links between the two countries, particularly the presence of Canadian pension funds and other institutional investors in India.The ministers discussed ways to make it easier for financial institutions and large investors from both countries to work together. They also looked at investment opportunities in sectors where both countries have common interests.The discussions included the need for domestic tax rules that provide "stability and certainty to taxpayers in respect of their investments".Financial technology and the wider financial sector were another major part of the talks. The two sides discussed cooperation in payments, financial stability, FinTech, capital markets and efforts to tackle financial crime.They agreed to encourage discussions between relevant authorities on cross-border remittances and payments made by merchants.Canada could also see wider use of India's Unified Payments Interface through partnerships between UPI and Canadian payment service providers.According to the joint statement, this could help deliver "faster, more efficient and cost-effective payments" and support trade, tourism, education and small and medium-sized businesses.India and Canada also discussed economic security and the need for reliable and diversified supply chains.Both sides agreed to explore cooperation in strategic areas, including critical minerals, which are important for industries such as clean energy, electronics and advanced technology.After the ministerial dialogue, Sitharaman and Champagne held joint discussions with representatives from Canada's financial services, FinTech, technology, artificial intelligence, infrastructure, and energy and natural resources sectors.The meetings focused on areas where businesses and financial institutions from both countries could increase long-term cooperation.The latest discussions come as economic ties between India and Canada have gained momentum in recent months. India-Canada merchandise trade was around USD 8 billion in 2025-26. India's exports to Canada stood at USD 4.67 billion, while imports were USD 3.28 billion, according to the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.The two countries are currently negotiating a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, or CEPA. They have set a separate target of increasing bilateral trade to USD 50 billion by 2030.Sitharaman is on an official visit to Canada and the United States from August 25 to September 2. During her time in Canada, she is also meeting Canadian businesses and taking part in investment and business roundtables focused on areas including energy, artificial intelligence and critical minerals.The next Canada-India Economic and Financial Dialogue is expected to be held in 2027. Both sides said they would continue regular discussions aimed at achieving "concrete cooperation and tangible outcomes" in areas of mutual interest.
Article Summary: India offers to begin talks with Canada on a Bilateral Investment Treaty at the earliest. Both countries aim to increase bilateral trade to CAD 70 billion, or INR 4.65 lakh crore, by 2030. Meeting follows commitment made by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Prime Minister Narendra Modi in March 2026.

Article Title: On F&O expiry day, sensex sees wild swings during Closing Auction Session
Article Text:
Sudden movement in closing period triggers outcry online.

‘Invest' 1 lakh at 3.15pm, make '44 lakh by 3.20pm’

On Thursday, within a five-minute window after the start of CAS on BSE—between 3.18pm and 3.23pm—sensex crashed over 2,200 points.

MUMBAI: In the first monthly expiry of derivatives contracts on BSE after the introduction of Closing Auction Session, popularly known as CAS, sensex and Bankex, BSE’s banking index, witnessed wild swings, triggering social media outcry. The sharp movement in indices and some of their constituents also gave rise to chances for some smart investors to make a killing.On Aug 3, Sebi introduced CAS, a new process of discovering the closing price of stocks that is used in several developed markets, aimed at eliminating chances of price manipulation.CAS is now valid for all those 200-odd stocks on which equity derivatives contracts are traded.For the rest of the non-derivatives stocks, the old system of volume-weighted average price (VWAP) continues. Since the launch of CAS, however, the two leading indices—Nifty and sensex—have witnessed extreme volatility and wide price variation between 3.15pm, just before CAS starts every session, and 3.30pm, when it ends.On Thursday, within a five-minute window after the start of CAS on BSE—between 3.18pm and 3.23pm—sensex crashed over 2,200 points and then within the next seven minutes—between 3.23pm and 3.30pm—it recovered nearly 2,000 points.It finally closed at 76,934 points, down 539 points from its Wednesday close.On NSE, things were relatively quiet. Between 3.18pm and 3.22pm, Nifty slid over 100 points but then recovered about 60 points to close 117 points lower at 24,091 points. On BSE, some of the leading stocks which are also sensex constituents witnessed huge volatility. During CAS, Reliance Industries, which has the highest weight in sensex, slid from Rs 1,289 to Rs 1,250, a drop of 3% within seven minutes, but then recovered equally sharply to close at Rs 1,286. Similar price swings were seen in HDFC Bank, ITC, Bharti Airtel and others.Traders continued to cry foul. On X (formerly Twitter), one trader pointed out that if someone had bought sensex put options of 76,500 worth Rs 1 lakh at 3.15pm and exited at 3.20pm, the trader’s profit in just five minutes would have been Rs 44 lakh.A week ago, Copthall Mauritius, a JP Morgan arm, was caught by Sebi, manipulating sensex and its constituents and for making illegal gains worth nearly Rs 3 crore. Sebi had alleged that domestic broker, Mansi Stock & Share Broking, indulged in a similar manipulation strategy. The regulator has banned Copthall and Mansi Broking (for proprietary trades only) from the market and ordered the two to disgorge illegal gains worth nearly Rs 3.8 crore.
Article Summary: Sensex and Bankex, BSE’s banking index, witnessed wild swings. The sharp movement in indices and some of their constituents also gave rise to chances for some smart investors to make a killing. On Aug 3, Sebi introduced CAS, a new process of discovering the closing price of stocks.

Article Title: HDFC looks to appeal 99.97% haircut on claims against Zee’s Chandra
Article Text:
Creditors filed claims of Rs 22,006 crore against Subhash Chandra for the loans he backed.

‘Was only a guarantor, did not borrow’

MUMBAI: With the National Company Law Tribunal this week clearing a repayment plan offering only Rs. 6.5 crore in a case concerning Zee Group’s Subhash Chandra’s personal guarantees for loans taken by his companies, HDFC Bank said it is exploring an appeal.Creditors filed claims of Rs. 22,006 crore against Subhash Chandra for the loans he backed, but the repayment plan approved by a majority of creditors and cleared by NCLT approves a 99.97% haircut — without impacting lender’s right to recover from the actual borrowers.Assenting creditors (80.8%) contested allegations of being related parties and argued that Rs. 6.5-crore plan offered a better outcome compared to pushing the personal guarantor into bankruptcy, since Chandra’s net worth according to the resolution professional was only Rs. 31.8 crore, of which Rs. 25 crore was his mortgaged house. Chandra has disputed the Rs. 22,000-crore liability, stating it reflected historical claims filed in 2022.Chandra put objecting creditors’ claims at Rs 3,992 crore, of which Rs 620 crore was settled, with borrowing entities offering another Rs 1,063–1,113 crore. The remaining Rs 16,201 crore of assenting claims was also being addressed by principal borrowers.He said he was only a personal guarantor and had not himself borrowed, adding that most of the guarantees were provided by him after group companies defaulted as lenders and made “emotional appeals” for guarantees, saying otherwise their employees would lose their jobs.The assenting creditors said even after the settlement, principal borrowers (group companies) continued to remain on the hook.HDFC’s Rs 698 crore claim represented 3.2% of the sum. Other dissenters, accounting for around 15%, include Axis Bank, Canara Bank, RBL Bank, Union Bank UK, IDBI Trusteeship and LIC Housing Finance.LIC Housing Finance said the order does not affect borrowers’ corporate liabilities or its security.The claims arise from Chandra’s personal guarantees for borrowings by Vivek Infracon, Spirit Textiles, and Churu Enterprises, as well as mortgage-backed facilities for Essel Corporate Resources and Jayneer Infrapower.The dissenting lenders argued that assenting creditors Veena Investments, Direct Media Distribution Ventures, World Crest Advisors, Lemonade Capital Advisors, and Corpcall Capital Advisors were related or associate entities and controlled 61.8% to 62% of voting rights, making them ineligible under Section 109(4)(b) of the IBC. They cited Veena’s control by Sushila Devi Goel, wife of Jawahar Goel, the personal guarantor’s brother, and links between partners of Lemonade and Corpcall and companies disclosed as related parties in Veena’s accounts.The 99.97% haircut headlines caught nationwide attention, with Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh stating: “The National Company Law Tribunal has just approved a repayment plan of a noted businessman under which creditors will receive only Rs 6.5 crores against admitted claims of around Rs 22,006.57 crore. This is not just a haircut. It is actually a mundan and makes a complete mockery of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code , 2016.”In a post on X, Vijay Mallya said, “If true, many congratulations to my friend Subhash,” contrasting the outcome with his own case by claiming banks and the govt had recovered Rs 14,100 crore against a Rs 6,203 crore judgment debt while continuing to pursue him, signing off with “Indian Debt Resolution Justice”.
Article Summary: HDFC Bank said it is exploring an appeal. Creditors filed claims of Rs 22,006 crore against Subhash Chandra for the loans he backed. Chandra has disputed the Rs. 22,000-crore liability, stating it reflected historical claims filed in 2022.

Article Title: HDFC shares drop 2% over CEO uncertainty, legal woes
Article Text:
HDFC shares drop 2% over CEO uncertainty, legal woes

MUMBAI: Shares of HDFC Bank fell 2% on Thursday, with analysts citing uncertainty over the appointment of its next CEO. The bank also faces legal action in the US over alleged violations of securities laws for not disclosing adverse information related to a bulk deposits case.HDFC Bank CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan’s tenure is set to expire on Oct 26. “There are just 2 months left and there is still no clarity about his extension/renewal. Markets have been worried about succession issues at HDFC Bank for some time now, as a result of which the stock has been weak,” said Suresh Ganapathy, an analyst with Macquarie.The appointment process requires the nomination and remuneration committee of the bank’s board to decide on candidates and recommend them to the board. RBI requires banks to send recommendations well before the CEO’s tenure ends.“In our opinion, there are two main options now, considering the paucity of time. Either the MD & CEO gets a tenure extension of say around 6 months or a full 3-year tenure. In case of the former, we believe, the messaging here is that the board is looking for candidates apart from the current CEO and wants time from RBI to recommend a new list. In case of latter, the uncertainty ends with respect to the CEO tenure,” Ganapathy said.He added that the stock could fall further if Jagdishan receives a short-term extension.Separately, the bank faces a federal securities class action lawsuit in New York. An investor’s complaint names the bank, its CEO and chief financial officer as defendants. The litigation follows a fall in the bank’s share price after allegations that HDFC Bank incentivised Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation with payments to attract bulk deposits. While the transaction may not have resulted in undue gains for individuals, RBI bars incentives for placing deposits.
Article Summary: HDFC Bank CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan’s tenure is set to expire on Oct 26. The bank also faces legal action in the US over alleged violations of securities laws for not disclosing adverse information related to a bulk deposits case.

Article Title: Centre goes all-out to woo Japanese companies for investment
Article Text:
Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal in conversation with ROHM Co. Ltd. President.

OSAKA: From focusing on high-tech industries to weaning away entities with presence in China and southeast Asia and wooing small Japanese banks, beyond the Big 3, that have strong local relationships, govt is deploying every tool to get Japanese firms to invest in India.The moves come amid heightened distrust with China, which has not just stopped supply of critical inputs needed by the Japanese industry, but has also indicated that profits can’t be repatriated to Japan and need to be invested there.India, officials said, is seen to be a reliable player, which has a democracy and rule of law, in addition to a large and growing market. The pitch is also that a base in India will also help tap the large talent pool as well as traditional trade relations with West Asia and Africa, which also boasts of a large Indian diaspora.“We are working with the regional and smaller banks to work in India,” India’s ambassador to Japan Nagma M Mallik said, adding that govt is keen to attract Japanese SME investment, which works closely with these lenders.A host of small players, from Yokohama Bank to The 77 Bank, Resona Bank and Toyoma Bank, operate in 47 prefectures, the first level of administration, and have close ties with local players. Many of the bankers also go on to be governors and wield influence.As a result, getting these banks can help open the doors to local businesses and SMEs, which are large in size compared to Indian standards and specialise in product segments.While some of the small banks are sending researchers to India, who will work with the three large Japanese banks, MUFG, SMBC and Mizuho, which have now established local presence through acquisitions, said another official.Separately, govt is hoping that just like Maruti brought in its vendors, the other large Japanese players will get its affiliates to set up shop in the country so that the entire value chain is covered.Japan is the fifth largest investor in India and govt is hoping that it will move up given the recent rush of investments, which have been focused more on the financial sector.
Article Summary: India, officials said, is seen to be a reliable player, which has a democracy and rule of law, in addition to a large and growing market. A base in India will also help tap the large talent pool as well as traditional trade relations with West Asia and Africa.

Article Title: Gaana, Fenix360 tie up to boost engagement
Article Text:
Streaming changed how the world listens to music. (Representative image)

MUMBAI: Gaana has partnered with social media and creator platform Fenix360 to build a more direct relationship between artists and their audiences by bringing content, community and commerce together within one ecosystem. At the centre of the integration will be a native scrolling social feed within Gaana, enabling artists to share visual content around their work while allowing fans to discover, follow and engage with them without having to move across multiple platforms.Streaming changed how the world listens to music. But for a long time, the relationship between artists and fans has largely stopped at the play button. Discovery happens on one platform, community happens on another and monetisation happens somewhere else if it happens at all. This partnership aims to close that gap.The wider ecosystem will also introduce new monetisation opportunities for artists. Through Fenix360’s tools, artists will be able to build digital storefronts, offer physical and digital merchandise, sell tickets to live shows, host gated and paid live streams, and receive direct financial support from their fans. A key part of the proposition is Fenix360’s creator-first monetisation model, under which artists will retain 70% of the revenue generated through its monetisation tools.
Article Summary: Gaana has partnered with social media and creator platform Fenix360 to build a more direct relationship between artists and their audiences. At the centre of the integration will be a native scrolling social feed within Gaana. The wider ecosystem will also introduce new monetisation opportunities for artists.

Article Title: ‘Govt to focus on easing processes to boost FDI’
Article Text:
Goyal has pitched India’s FTAs as an opportunity for investors to make use of and export to other countries.

Focus on value chain, KYC

No decision on CPTPP, focus on FTAs

Strong growth in Q1

Japan’s demand

Commerce & industry minister Piyush Goyal Thursday said govt will focus on easing processes and faster clearances, wherever required, to boost FDI flows, while asserting that Indian economy has seen a robust expansion in first quarter, for which data is due to be released next week.“We are open to ideas, whatever industry demands… there’s tremendous scope to improve process, procedure and policy to help faster flow of FDI and to help give comfort to investors about the fact that their investments will lead to production and productive activity faster,” the minister said. He added that faster and more efficient KYC norms and mutual recognition agreements with regulators from other countries are required so that approvals on both sides are recognised and there could be some areas for simplification.Goyal said govt was keen that investment model should not only focus on large companies but the entire value chain that leads to downstream indigenisation. In paints, for instance, import of titanium dioxide, a key input, is of the tune of $1 billion and govt wants it to be manufactured in India, he said.Similarly, the idea is to go beyond semiconductors and promote production of gases, specialty chemicals, equipment, components, so that the value chain goes beyond design and testing or assembly.“So, our effort is more and more going deep dive, becoming self-reliant, and also creating more jobs.”Goyal has pitched India’s FTAs as an opportunity for investors to make use of and export to other countries, in addition to making in India for domestic market. While stating that more FTAs – from Canada and Chile to Israel and the South African Customs Union -- are under negotiation, he said there is no decision on Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) – the 11-nation trading bloc that includes Japan, Australia, Canada, Chile, Malaysia and Singapore. “A lot of people are asking us to consider this suggestion. We have not yet really applied our mind to it.”“The reports I am getting from industry seem to suggest that the first quarter has gone quite well. Export has been up 15%. So, my own sense is the first quarter will once again give very good results. Despite all the global uncertainties and challenges, we were the fastest-growing large economy last year, probably the first quarter will continue to show that India is a resilient nation, on the move,” he said.Goyal said that while FTAs open doors to overseas markets, there is a large domestic economy that companies can tap. While trade with West Asia is normalising, Goyal said that efforts are underway to open new routes on the eastern sides, be it oil and gas pipelines or train lines.The minister said that Japan has demanded restoration of benefit for a chemical that is used in the semiconductor value chain and govt will seek to ensure that the benefit, which was withdrawn due to misuse, is tapped properly.
Article Summary: Commerce & industry minister Piyush Goyal said govt will focus on easing processes and faster clearances, wherever required, to boost FDI flows. Goyal has pitched India’s FTAs as an opportunity for investors to make use of and export to other countries. While stating that more FTAs – from Canada and Chile to Israel and the South African Customs Union – are under negotiation, he said there is no decision on Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans- Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)

Article Title: Actor Sunny Leone cleared in Rs 70L commission dispute case
Article Text:
A sessions court dismissed a criminal plea against Sunny Leone and others.





MUMBAI: A sessions court has dismissed a criminal revision plea against actor Sunny Leone (Karenjit Kaur Vohra), her husband Daniel Weber and their manager Sunny Rajani in a dispute over alleged unpaid commission of more than Rs 70 lakh for a Telugu film, holding that a commercial breach cannot be treated as a criminal offence unless fraudulent or dishonest intention exists from the outset.Complainant Omprakash Jain had approached the sessions court after a magistrate's court dismissed his private complaint in 2024. He had alleged cheating, criminal breach of trust and criminal intimidation, claiming Sunny Leone was given a role in the film through his efforts. Jain said there was an understanding that the accused would pay him a 10% incentive from the Rs 1.75 crore consideration connected with the engagement, but he received only part payment.According to the complaint, after Sunny Leone received Rs 35 lakh, Jain was paid Rs 1.75 lakh on Nov 26, 2000. He further claimed Rs 3.5 lakh was paid on July 20, 2022, but the balance amount of Rs 70 lakh and the corresponding 10% incentive were withheld.The record showed Jain had earlier sought an inquiry through the magistrate's court. On Dec 6, 2023, the magistrate refused to order a police investigation and directed him to proceed with verification under Section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.In revision, Jain argued that the magistrate had failed to apply proper mind, wrongly treated the matter as civil, and rejected the complaint despite material allegedly showing cheating, fraud and breach of trust.Weber, Leone and Rajani, through advocate Rajkumar Mishra, opposed the plea, saying the complaint did not disclose the ingredients of offence.Additional Sessions Judge P A Sane noted that the documents included a tax invoice, two Form 16-A copies and a full-and-final settlement document in Jain's favour. The court said these reflected a commercial transaction. Even if non-payment was accepted, it said, that alone did not establish cheating or breach of trust.
Article Summary: Complainant Omprakash Jain had approached the sessions court after a magistrate's court dismissed his private complaint in 2024. He had alleged cheating, criminal breach of trust and criminal intimidation, claiming Sunny Leone was given a role in the film through his efforts.

Article Title: It’s official: Kerala is now ‘Keralam’ as Centre notifies name change
Article Text:
The Union home ministry has officially notified Keralam as the new name for the southern state (Representative image)





KOCHI: The Union home ministry has notified ' Keralam ' as the new name of the southern state, with the change coming into effect from Tuesday.In a gazette notification issued on Tuesday, the home ministry said, “In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (2) of Section 1 of the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026, the Central government hereby appoints the 25th day of August, 2026, as the date on which the provisions of the said Act shall come into force.”Earlier this month, President Droupadi Murmu gave her assent to a Bill seeking to rename Kerala as Keralam, turning the legislation into law, news agency PTI reported.The Lok Sabha passed the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill on August 11, followed by the Rajya Sabha on August 12.In the Rajya Sabha, minister of state for home affairs Nityanand Rai said the Kerala Assembly had passed a resolution in 2024 urging the Centre to introduce legislation to change the state's name to Keralam.“The Bill provides that the state of Kerala will be known as the state of Keralam, and hence there is a proposal to rename Kerala to Keralam,” he said.The Kerala government had forwarded the state Assembly's resolution on the proposed name change to the Centre in June 2024, PTI reported.Subsequently, President Murmu referred the Bill to the state legislature for its views, following which the Assembly unanimously adopted a resolution agreeing with the Bill.The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act changes the state's name, along with the necessary amendments to the Constitution and consequential provisions.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: The Union home ministry has officially notified Keralam as the new name for the southern state. Earlier this month, President Droupadi Murmu gave her assent to a Bill seeking to rename Kerala. The change comes into effect from Tuesday.

Article Title: US debt crosses $40 trillion: But who does Uncle Sam owe money to?
Article Text:
Trump is adding to a US debt pile that has been building for decades under both parties.

What is national debt, anyway?

At around 124% of US GDP, the $40tn debt pile is larger than the entire annual economic output of the country.

So who does Uncle Sam actually owe?

At around 124% of US GDP, the $40tn debt pile is larger than the entire annual economic output of the country.

Trump's debt bill so far

Trump’s second-term debt accumulation is already moving faster than during his first term

The bond market's verdict

The pace of borrowing has changed dramatically: the latest $1tn was added in less than five months, compared with 205 years for the first.

The bill keeps coming

Forty trillion dollars. Written out in full, that is $40,000,000,000,000, a four followed by thirteen zeros.Spend a dollar every second, and it would take more than 1.2 million years to get through the whole amount. Or stack that same sum in $100 bills, one on top of the other, and the pile would reach around 27,000 miles into the sky, enough to wrap right around the Earth with room to spare.On August 18, the US Treasury confirmed that America's national debt had crossed exactly that mark for the first time in history, months earlier than most forecasters expected just a year ago. That works out to roughly $117,000 for every American, or nearly $297,000 per household.Numbers this size stop meaning much after a while. But they raise one genuinely interesting question. Who does the world's biggest economy owe to?Every year a government spends more than it collects in tax, the shortfall is called a deficit. Governments cover that gap by borrowing, mostly by selling Treasury bonds, bills and notes to investors. Add up enough years of deficits and you end up with a national debt.Think of it like a mortgage or a business loan. Borrowing money is not automatically reckless.What matters is what the money is spent on, and whether the economy grows quickly enough to make the borrowing worthwhile.Countries have used debt for centuries to fund wars, recover from crises, and build the infrastructure and technology that drive future growth. If the economy grows faster than the cost of borrowing, the debt becomes easier to carry over time. That is roughly what happened after the Second World War. Debt held by the public reached around 106% of GDP, then decades of strong postwar growth steadily brought the ratio down, without America ever needing to pay off the whole debt in one go.Japan shows just how much debt an advanced economy can carry without collapsing. Its debt-to-GDP ratio sits above 200%, the highest of any major economy, and has done for years. Most of that debt is held domestically and in yen, which shields Japan from the kind of panic that hits countries reliant on foreign lenders.America has a similar cushion. The dollar is the world's dominant reserve currency, and US Treasuries are seen as one of the world's safest assets, which keeps investors willing to lend Washington money.The real concern is not that America has debt. It is the maths behind it. Interest rates have climbed sharply since 2022, and the cost of servicing the debt is now rising faster than the economy itself, a very different picture to the cheap-borrowing years of the 2010s.This is where the $40tn figure gets interesting.Start with the $7.78tn in intragovernmental debt, roughly a fifth of the total. Think of it as the government moving money from one of its own pockets to another. The largest holder is the Social Security Trust Fund, which holds around $2.3tn. When payroll taxes bring in more than the programme pays out in benefits, the surplus is invested in special Treasury securities, essentially one arm of government holding an IOU from another.The remaining $32.27tn is debt held by the public, and this is where the "who does America owe" question really begins.The biggest slice belongs to domestic private investors. American mutual funds, banks, insurers, pension funds and households collectively hold around $17.9tn, or roughly 57% of publicly held debt. If you have a pension or an index fund with any bond exposure, there is a decent chance you are quietly one of Uncle Sam's creditors yourself.The Federal Reserve holds a further $4.4-4.5tn through its own bond portfolio, close to 14%.Foreign investors hold around $9.35tn, roughly 29% of publicly held debt, and less than a quarter of the full $40tn once intragovernmental debt is included.Here the popular image usually gets it wrong. China is not the biggest foreign holder, and has not been for years. That title belongs to Japan, a close US ally, which holds around $1.21tn. The UK comes second at roughly $937bn. China sits third at around $651bn, having steadily cut its exposure from a 2013 peak of $1.32tn as Beijing diversifies its reserves. Further down the list sit Belgium, the Cayman Islands, Luxembourg and Ireland, all financial centres, so their large holdings often belong to investors based elsewhere entirely, simply routed through custodians there.The US Treasury does not owe these countries one giant loan. It owes millions of investors through a constantly rolling market of Treasury securities. Even Japan's $1.21tn holding is nowhere near enough to dictate America's borrowing costs on its own.Add it up and roughly four-fifths of America's $40tn is owed to Americans, American institutions or the government itself.The popular image of America being indebted to the rest of the world is therefore misleading. Uncle Sam’s debt is overwhelmingly homegrown.Since Trump returned to office in January 2025, the debt has grown by around $3.8tn in about nineteen months. Combined with the $7.8tn added in his first term, his two terms have so far added roughly $11.6tn. For comparison, the debt grew by about $8.4tn across Joe Biden's four years, from roughly $27.8tn to $36.2tn, so the current pace is running noticeably faster.A large chunk of the recent rise came from the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, the tax and spending package Trump signed into law in July 2025, which the Congressional Budget Office estimates will add around $4tn to the deficit over the next decade, largely through extended tax cuts. Rising defence spending, including the cost of this year's war with Iran, has added further pressure, alongside the lost tariff revenue outlined earlier.But the debt problem does not belong to one president. The US has run persistent deficits under both parties for decades, through tax cuts, wars, recessions and emergency spending. The $40tn figure is simply the accumulated bill.The $40tn figure tells us how much America owes. The bond market helps determine how much it costs to keep owing it.Think of the US government as someone with a giant mortgage that never quite gets paid off. Every time part of that mortgage comes due, it borrows again to pay it off. As long as lenders are happy to keep offering roughly the same interest rate, the arrangement can continue without too much trouble.The problem starts when those lenders ask for more.That is essentially what Treasury yields tell us. A Treasury yield is the interest rate investors demand to lend money to the US government. When yields rise, Washington has to pay more to borrow. And because the US has to keep refinancing huge amounts of existing debt while borrowing more to cover its deficit, even a small increase in rates can eventually add billions to the government's interest bill.That is why the bond market matters to the $40tn story.On the day the debt crossed $40tn, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced plans to at least double some long-term Treasury buyback operations, from $2bn to at least $4bn per operation. The move came as a bond sell-off pushed the 30-year Treasury yield as high as 5.34%, its highest level since 2007.The announcement briefly pushed yields lower before they drifted back up within a day. That is because a buyback can help manage the supply of bonds in the market, but it does not fix the underlying deficit. It is more like rearranging the mortgage than reducing the amount you owe.The reason investors are jumpy is in the numbers. The federal deficit is running at around 5.8% of GDP, well above the 3.8% average of the past 50 years. Interest costs alone eat up about 3.3% of GDP and are now one of the fastest-growing items in the federal budget.The risk is a feedback loop. If borrowing costs stay above the pace at which the economy grows, the debt becomes harder to stabilise. Rising interest costs can then require more borrowing, putting further pressure on rates.America's first trillion dollars of debt took 205 years to accumulate, arriving in October 1981. The most recent trillion, the climb from $39tn to $40tn, took under five months. Ten trillion came in 2008, twenty trillion in 2017, thirty trillion in 2022, and now forty trillion in 2026, each milestone arriving faster than the last.None of that means the sky is falling. America can still borrow in its own currency, and investors around the world still buy its debt when markets turn nervous. What has changed is the price of that comfort.The $40tn figure is not a crisis on its own. It is the accumulated bill for decades of tax cuts, wars, recessions and political promises made by presidents and Congresses of both parties.The US can keep rolling the debt over. But the interest bill keeps coming due.
Article Summary: The $40tn debt pile is larger than the entire annual economic output of the country. It would take more than 1.2 million years to get through the whole amount. The largest holder is the Social Security Trust Fund, which holds around $2.3tn.

Article Title: 'Time to teach Canada': Trump rails as trade war gets ugly
Article Text:
Trump warns Canada amid tariff dispute

US president Donald Trump has warned Canada of possible further action, saying it was “time to teach Canada you can't do this anymore,” as trade tensions between the two countries intensify.Canada on Tuesday announced retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on more than 700 US products worth around $27.6 billion, escalating its trade dispute with the United States.Canadian prime minister Mark Carney accused Washington of seeking to subordinate Canada, saying US demands during the failed trade negotiations showed that Americans wanted to “destroy our major industries”, including autos, steel and aluminium.The new tariffs, set to take effect on September 8, will cover a broad range of American goods, including fish, cheese, honey, cosmetics, clothing, household appliances, smartphones, motorcycles, and steel and aluminium products.The tariffs will be imposed at rates of 15%, 25% and 50%, with the highest rate applying to several products, including certain dairy, cosmetics and lumber items. Canada will also increase tariffs on US steel and aluminium products from 25% to 50%, CBC News reported.Ottawa said the measures target products “most affected by US tariffs” and are intended to match the duties imposed by Washington in its latest round of tariffs.Canada’s latest measures extend beyond industrial goods, targeting everyday products such as cheese, toilet paper, clothing, smartphones and household appliances.Trade tensions have continued to escalate, with Trump threatening further tariffs on Canadian vehicles, auto parts and steel.He said his administration would raise tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts and steel to 50% from January 1, 2027.Carney said the proposed auto tariffs would “gradually dismantle” Canada’s vehicle production industry.Trump also added another point of friction on Tuesday, saying the US was giving “serious consideration” to renaming Lake Ontario as “Lake America”, amid his ongoing dispute with Ontario Premier Doug Ford.
Article Summary: Canada announces retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on more than 700 US products worth around $27.6 billion. New tariffs, set to take effect on September 8, will cover a broad range of American goods. Canada will also increase tariffs on US steel and aluminium products from 25% to 50%.

Article Title: Fastest growing global finance super app Abound chooses Monad to power its next phase of growth
Article Text:
Abound plans to launch a new wallet that will allow users to transfer money between US and Indian bank accounts

Abound, a financial services platform for Indians in the US backed by Times Internet, has crossed $500 million in remittance volumes over the past year.The platform, which initially focused on helping users send money to India, has expanded into a broader financial services app for the Indian diaspora in the US. Its services include cross-border transfers, savings and other financial and lifestyle benefits.Abound said it now plans to expand its services to Indians living in other countries and introduce products aimed at helping users manage their finances across borders.As part of its next phase, Abound plans to launch a new wallet that will allow users to transfer money between US and Indian bank accounts and manage multi-currency balances in one place.The wallet is expected to launch in the third quarter of 2026, with a waitlist opening soon. The company said it also plans to add support for more countries.Abound is also planning new savings and investment products, including accounts that offer interest, giving non-resident Indians (NRIs) more options to manage and invest their money.The company also plans to introduce AI-powered features to automate parts of users' financial activities.These will include workflows using the x402 payment protocol, which is designed to support payments made through AI agents.Nishkaam Mehta, CEO of Abound, said the company had moved $500 million since its launch and that its next phase would focus on helping NRIs manage more aspects of their financial lives."Abound has become the platform Indians in the US trust to move money home; we have moved $500 million since launch," Mehta said.Monad, a Layer 1 blockchain platform, will provide the technology infrastructure for Abound's upcoming products. The company said Monad's technology would support its plans to expand services to the global Indian diaspora.Raj Parekh, head of Payments & Stablecoins at Monad Foundation, said Abound was beginning an "ambitious journey" to build a wider range of financial services for NRIs."With its distribution through the Times of India, Abound is starting an ambitious journey to provide a complete suite of agentic financial services and a cross-border platform for NRIs. We're thrilled to watch Abound use Monad's technology to assist them advance into the next phase of their endeavors," Parekh stated.The partnership is expected to form the technology base for Abound's next phase as the company expands beyond remittances and develops more cross-border financial services.
Article Summary: Abound plans to launch a new wallet that will allow users to transfer money between US and Indian bank accounts.
